Check the current RightShip methodology and the vessel's verified EVDI, EEXI and GHG data.

Bayrak devletine veya RO'ya raporlanan D.en: DCS data reported to the flag state or RO are anonymized by IMO and published in an aggregated form in the IMO GISIS database; Although anonymization hides the identity of the individual ship, it allows the creation of comparative performance tables across the industry by ship type, size and age categories. This global transparency has enabled DCS to transform from a mere regulatory obligation into a commercial pressure tool: charterers and cargo owners are questioning DCS-based efficiency indicators (CII rating, AER trends) when choosing ships to charter, preferring low carbon intensity among similar ships, and some large cargo owners are imposing a minimum CII rating requirement in their contracts. Thus, a ship's DCS data has turned into a performance card that plays a role not only in flag state control but also in its ability to earn freight in the free market; Poor data quality or low ratings are also commercially costly.

CSS Code'un Ek 13 hesaplama yöntemi, gem.en: The Annex 13 calculation method of the CSS Code is based on numerically estimating the inertial force that ship motion exerts on the load. When the ship rolls and pitches at sea, every point on the deck is subjected to an angular acceleration and a corresponding linear acceleration; This acceleration is multiplied by the weight of the load at that point to obtain horizontal and vertical inertia forces, and the net force trying to shift or topple the load is calculated in this way. The most critical parameter of the calculation is the ship's metacentric height (GM): a ship with a high GM behaves 'stiff', that is, completes the roll quickly and with large angular acceleration, which magnifies the inertial forces on the deck load; A 'soft' (tender) ship with a low GM will make slower and larger rolls, the acceleration will be smaller, but an extremely low GM is dangerous in terms of stability. Therefore, lashing design must take into calculation the GM range of the ship in expected loading situations; The same load and the same lashing arrangement may have different safety margins at different GM values. Annex 13 formulates this relationship with standard motion coefficients and design wave conditions to produce the minimum cargo securing capacity required for each load position.

DR dış etkisiz hesap mevkidir; EP dış et.en: Dead reckoning (DR) advances a previous position using course steered and distance through the water. An estimated position (EP) also allows for estimated current and leeway. Neither replaces an independently established fix.

Kodun teknik özü, tahıl kaymasından doğa.en: The technical essence of the code is to calculate the heeling moment resulting from grain shifting and prove that the ship's stability reserve is sufficient against this. There are certain numerical thresholds: the angle of heel resulting from shearing must not exceed a certain limit (about 12° or the angle of entry of the deck edge into the water, whichever is smaller) and the remaining dynamic stability area must not fall below a minimum value (0.075 m·rad). The calculation is made with different space assumptions for partially filled and fully filled cargo holds. The ship must carry an approved grain loading booklet containing these calculation and a Document of Authorization showing grain transportation competence.

Kuralın yetersiz kaldığı durumlar: (a) G.en: Cases where the rule fails: (a) Tidal period other than six hours: in some areas the HW–LW interval is 5 hours or 7–8 hours; The 6-hour rates of the rule give incorrect results in these ports. (b) Asymmetric tidal profile: in some ports the rising tide may be fast and the falling tide slow (or vice versa); The rule of 12 cannot capture this asymmetry. (c) Critical UKC calculation: the rule of 12 is not sufficient in calculation with narrow safety margins; tidal curve should be used.

, yükleme operasyonlarının ayna görüntüs.en: Although it may seem like a mirror image of loading operations, it carries additional risks. During unloading, the ship's displacement decreases; Therefore, the KM value changes and GM may decrease unexpectedly. Additionally, adequate propeller immersion must be ensured, minimum draft requirements must be met and trim control must be maintained. Discharging too quickly, unbalanced discharging and delayed ballast removal are the most common hazards.

Regulation 20 – Double hull tankers: A d.en: MARPOL Annex I regulations 19 and 20 address double-hull requirements and phase-out arrangements for applicable oil tankers. Ship size, construction date and the detailed provisions determine applicability; one DWT threshold is not a complete compliance test.
